correctness.rationale: Every inverse Lyndon length-k word has a unique unbordered anti-Lyndon primitive root of length m<=k, and maximal border k-m. Counting primitive necklaces by Mobius inversion gives exact histograms. Prefix closure and finite integer tail summation give exact random-array expectations; q-ary asymptotics and exponential tail domination yield the sharp harmonic coefficient and geometric limit. Two independent exhaustive descriptions agree for all binary words up to length 12 and ternary up to length 8. Proof does not rely on finite checks.

originality.rationale: The known 2018 anti-Lyndon root classification is a strict predecessor and explicitly credited. The new combined claim derives an exact border histogram and conditional geometric limit plus a sharp harmonic random-prefix law and \(n\log n\) expected inverse-array entry mass. Four directly relevant primary full texts were inspected. Published related random string statistics concern distinct substrings or subsequence universality, not this array. Unindexed equivalents remain a residual risk.
